archetype.name: Dual-Threat (designed-run)
archetype.definition: A young starter whose value rests as much on called quarterback runs as on his arm, paired with a quicker, more on-schedule passing game than he showed as a rookie.

report.headline: One brilliant game against a bad defense, then buried at QB4
report.take:
Jaxson Dart's 2026 line is mostly one afternoon. Against Dallas in Week 1 he went 23/29 for 230 yards and 3 touchdowns, added 54 rushing yards, and posted 21.9 passing EPA. That game is why he ranks 2nd of 47 in EPA per dropback (0.578) and 1st in completion rate. In Week 2 at the Rams he played 12% of the snaps, threw five passes, and did not practice the following week. Jameis Winston started Weeks 3 through 6 and J.J. McCarthy started Week 7. As of November 3 the depth chart lists Dart fourth. The efficiency numbers are real, but they describe a quarterback who is not currently playing.

The Week 1 tape still says something. He got the ball out faster than as a rookie (2.64 seconds to throw against 2.82) and his bad-throw rate fell from 15% to 11.8%. His best work came between the numbers and past the sticks: 11 intermediate attempts at 1.167 EPA each, 9 third-down throws converting 88.9%, and 7 red-zone attempts that produced all 3 touchdowns. Isaiah Likely was the main beneficiary, at 1.357 EPA per target. The designed runs carried over from 2025, when his 487 rushing yards ranked 3rd among quarterbacks: 6 called runs at 8.17 yards a carry, none stuffed.

The context deflates the numbers. Dallas now ranks 32nd in defensive EPA, so the showcase came against the league's worst unit. The first test against a good one (the Rams, 4th) ended almost before it began. The sample is 34 attempts. Some of what looked like growth runs against his history: his 2025 CPOE ranked 35th of 63, and he has gone 0-for-3 on deep throws this year. One trait held firm. His pressure-to-sack rate ranks 28th of 38 after ranking 43rd of 62 last year, so he still takes sacks when pressure gets home.

From here, the question is whether he plays at all, not how well. He was a first-round pick in his second year, and a run-heavy Harbaugh offense (30th in pass rate over expected) has used three starters. A path back exists if the veterans falter. Until the depth chart changes, treat him as a stash with an encouraging but thin 2026 resume.

strengths.title: Designed runs that reliably gain yards
strengths.body: Called quarterback runs are the steadiest part of his game. He was a top-three rushing quarterback as a rookie, and his six designed runs this year averaged 8.17 yards with a perfect success rate. That comes from scheme plus size and speed rather than scrambling luck, so it is the skill most likely to travel whenever he plays again.

strengths.title: Intermediate accuracy and situational finishing
strengths.body: In Week 1 he lived in the 10-19 yard window and converted almost every money down: 1.167 EPA per intermediate attempt, nearly every third down moved, and a perfect red zone. Quicker processing and fewer bad throws than in 2025 support part of this. The red-zone and third-down rates come from single-digit attempts against the worst defense in football and will come down hard.

concerns.title: He has lost the job entirely
concerns.body: He left Week 2 after 12% of the snaps, missed practice the next week, and the Giants have since started Winston and then McCarthy. Now he sits fourth on the depth chart. Whatever the reason, the organization has moved on for now, and his stats are frozen at a two-game sample.

concerns.title: Production came against the worst defense
concerns.body: Essentially all of his positive EPA came against Dallas, now ranked last in defensive EPA. Against the 4th-ranked Rams he managed 20 yards on five throws. Read the league-best efficiency ranks as a ceiling sighting, not a baseline.

concerns.title: Sacks under pressure, no deep game
concerns.body: His pressure-to-sack rate was among the worst as a rookie and is still bottom-third this year. That is a persistent trait, and with only two scrambles it isn't being repaid by off-script yards. He also completed none of his three deep shots. Both point to a passer who is better on schedule than off it.

trend.note: He opened with a near-perfect game against Dallas, was pulled from Week 2 after a handful of snaps, and has fallen from starter to QB4 without taking another meaningful snap.

nextGame.headline: Soft Eagles defense, but Dart isn't in line to play
nextGame.body:
On paper Philadelphia is exactly what a Dart-style quarterback wants. The Eagles rank 29th in defensive EPA, 24th against the pass and 31st against the run. They are dead last in both QB hit rate and sack rate, which would cover his habit of taking sacks under pressure. Their run defense would also invite the designed keepers. The Giants are 3.5-point favorites off a bye in a 40.5-point total, which projects a controlled, run-leaning script.

None of that reaches him unless the depth chart changes. He is listed fourth behind the quarterbacks who have started the last five games, so the realistic projection is zero snaps. On the Giants' side, Cam Skattebo (questionable, hamstring) and backup tackle Marcus Mbow matter to whoever starts. Philadelphia's secondary is thin, with Jonathan Jones out, Jakorian Bennett on IR and Michael Carter II questionable. That helps the Giants' starter, not Dart.

keyMatchups.title: No pass rush to punish holding
keyMatchups.body: Philadelphia generates the fewest sacks and hits in the league. A quarterback with Dart's sack tendency would have time to work the intermediate middle where he thrived in Week 1. This only applies if he plays.

keyMatchups.title: Leaky run defense vs designed runs
keyMatchups.body: The Eagles' 31st-ranked run defense is the kind of front his called runs exploited against Dallas. Any package snaps for Dart would most plausibly come here.

nextGame.watch: Whether Dart moves up the depth chart or dresses at all; anything beyond inactive or emergency QB would be news.

restOfSeason.body:
The base case is that Dart stays behind the veterans and adds little or nothing to his 2026 line, roughly 0-15 passing yards a game in his current role. If he gets the job back, expect his Week 1 efficiency to come down a long way. The 76.5% completion rate, perfect red zone and near-perfect third downs came on tiny samples against the league's worst defense. His 2025 baseline was a mid-pack passer with top-tier rushing. A realistic starter line is around 170-215 passing yards, 1.0-1.6 touchdowns and 30-45 rushing yards a game. The quicker release and lower bad-throw rate may stick. The run game will.

What would sustain value: the designed-run package, which has held across both seasons, and the progress in getting the ball out on time. What will regress: the touchdown rate, the third-down and red-zone perfection, and the zero interceptions. He threw five in 12 games as a rookie.

projections.stat: Passing yards / game (if he regains the start)

swingFactors: Whether the Giants turn back to him over Winston and McCarthy
Sack rate when facing real pressure

confidence.note: 34 attempts, one real game against the worst defense, and now fourth on the depth chart.
